title: Impulse Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes: Equivalence of Degeneracy and Code-Shortening
authors: Shobhit Bhatnagar, Michele Pacenti, Nithin Raveendran, David Declercq, Bane Vasić
abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for building scalable quantum computers. Within the stabilizer formalism, the Calderbank-Shor-Steane framework constructs quantum codes from pairs of classical linear codes. A distinctive feature in this setting is degeneracy, where multiple equivalent error estimates exist-a phenomenon that has no classical counterpart, and the lack of a meaningful classical coding-theoretic interpretation of which has remained a gap in the literature. In this paper, we demonstrate that degeneracy is closely related to the classical operation of shortening of a linear block code. Interestingly, the shortening here takes place at the decoder rather than at the encoder. Leveraging this insight, we present a parallel decoding scheme for quantum low-density parity-check codes, which we term impulse decoding, that significantly outperforms belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding, as well as several other existing techniques, under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise, with significantly lesser complexity. We then present another algorithm based on decoding of residual errors, which when combined with impulse decoding achieves further performance improvement under circuit-level noise.
summary: This paper develops advanced decoding algorithms, notably impulse decoding, for Quantum LDPC codes by establishing a novel link: quantum degeneracy is equivalent to classical code shortening. The proposed methods significantly improve error correction performance and reduce complexity compared to prior state-of-the-art techniques under realistic noise models.
main_problem: The paper addresses quantum degeneracy in Quantum Error Correction (QEC) within stabilizer codes, which lacks a clear classical coding-theoretic interpretation.
main_result: It establishes that quantum degeneracy is mathematically equivalent to the classical operation of code shortening performed at the decoder. A novel decoding scheme called impulse decoding significantly outperforms existing methods under various noise conditions.
method: The authors develop and compare multiple parallel decoding schemes, including impulse decoding and residual-error decoding, by leveraging the theoretical link between quantum degeneracy and classical code shortening.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes constructed using the stabilizer formalism from pairs of classical linear codes (CSS codes). Performance is tested using specific examples like the [[288, 12, 18]] BB code.
key_observables: Failure rate vs. physical error rate; logical error rates; decoding latency; and computational complexity relative to existing decoders.
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($p$); number of parallel decoders ($N$); maximum residual error rounds ($R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that restricting the search space via code shortening (e.g., fixing $\hat{e}_1=0$) is sufficient to maintain correctness while reducing complexity.
figures_summary: Figures compare impulse decoding performance against Belief Propagation variants, showing superior error correction capability; they also illustrate how limiting variable node shortening to a subset maintains high performance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical link between degeneracy and code shortening. It then introduces Impulse Decoding as a parallel scheme based on this insight. Finally, it presents advanced variations combining impulse decoding with residual error correction for improved noise resilience.
why_interesting: While focused on QEC theory, the rigorous mathematical connection drawn between quantum degeneracy and classical coding concepts like 'shortening' provides deep insights into the underlying algebraic structure of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
